arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Arizona argues the National Voter Registration Act does not preempt Proposition 200.
The state claims Congress did not expressly prohibit state enforcement of citizenship rules.
The Inter Tribal Council argues the federal form streamlines the registration process.
The challengers assert federal law preempts state-added documentary requirements.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The dispute involves the National Voter Registration Act. Arizona enacted Proposition 200. This measure requires documentary proof of citizenship. Federal law requires a signed attestation. The state argues federal law does not preempt its stricter rule. The challengers argue federal law preempts the state requirement.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The outcome defines the boundary between state and federal voter registration authority. It determines whether states can impose stricter citizenship documentation rules. This affects the uniformity of federal voter registration processes nationwide.
